pro_course_detail.title: Fun English Conversation Practice with a Native Speaker
pro_course_detail.description:
Practice your English with a native speaker! We can discuss current events & culture, books & films, or practice scenarios you might encounter—like preparing for an interview, or traveling in the United States. I especially love to talk about traveling, if you're preparing for a big trip!

Throughout our conversation, I will take note of your English level and give you grammar tips, phrases to practice, useful slang, and help you better construct your sentences. I will also direct you toward resources to improve your speaking, writing, reading, and listening skills in between classes.

pro_course_detail.title: Pronunciation & Accent Practice 🎤
pro_course_detail.description:
Talk like an American! Whether you want to improve your ability to communicate clearly with native speakers, imitate your favorite American TV stars, or sound more natural in your everyday speech—great accent ability begins with learning to listen, to hear the subtle differences between sounds and learn to mimic them yourself. In this class, we focus on three main areas of accent training:

(1) Pronunciation, particularly English short vowels and difficult consonants,
(2) Intonation, or the "music" of the language,
(3) Connected speech, or how to link and blend words naturally like an American English speaker,
(4) Common native expressions and filler words.

To begin, I'll analyze your current speech level and identify target areas to strengthen your pronunciation. At the sentence level, we'll look at how the English language stresses its words, and discuss the difference between stress-timed and syllable-timed resources. We'll also identify patterns in the ways that native English speakers blend their words when speaking casually (which should help you better understand TV shows and movies!) To round it all out, we'll practice including some common expressions and filler language in your speech, especially while speaking casually.

Lessons are tailored to each individual student. I draw upon a variety of resources to help to develop your speech skills, and will include sound clips for you to practice what we learn in each session. You can do it—let's have fun with accents!

pro_course_detail.title: English Writing & Grammar 📝
pro_course_detail.description:
In this class, we focus on improving grammar and writing in the English language. Phrasal verbs, past perfect verb tenses, zero conditionals, and more! We will use short and long writing exercises (depending on the student's goals and preferences) to practice the grammar you're studying. As a writer, I love playing with words, finding the best way to express an idea, and I want to convey that grammatical enthusiasm over to you! 🤓📝

Short exercise: Compose a series of sentences using the target grammar in our lesson (for example, one sentence for each of the twelve English verb tenses). Then in class, we'll review the nuances and differences in meaning, both implied and explicit, by tweaking the words.

Long exercise: Write a short paragraph (100-500 words) telling me about a day in your life, a short story or essay, or an opinion of a book or TV show that you've recently watched. Anything that interests you! Then, during class, we will review your writing and correct it for grammar, language use, clarity, and word choice. We will discuss the differences in professional versus casual tone. This is a good class for students wanting to improve their essay-writing, professionals wanting to improve their email communications, and all other writers wanting to improve their command of English.

pro_course_detail.title: Business English 💼
pro_course_detail.description: In this class, we'll review the ways that English in the workplace can differ from friendly conversational English between friends; business English often uses a different set of vocabulary terms, idioms, and higher register of formality and politeness. We'll explore different ways to write an email, have conversations with your boss, and talk in meetings, with a bit of situational role play for you to practice! I draw upon my own experience working professionally as an architect, and I also encourage students to bring in examples of real-life language they encounter at their job, so we can discuss situations specific to their jobs and careers. Let's dive in!

pro_course_detail.title: English for Kids (Ages 4-15) 🎈
pro_course_detail.description:
Fun conversational classes for kids! Let them try out their English in a friendly, relaxed environment (this is the best way for anyone to learn, but especially children). I encourage them to talk about their interests, hobbies, favorite characters and toys. They can tell me about life in their home country, and ask questions about the United States and American culture! Depending on their skill level and interests, we'll learn new vocabulary, read some children's stories together, and play some grammar games to advance their English level.

I began my ESL career teaching English online to children in China and have taught over 2750 classes to over 1200 students, ages 4-15, predominantly 8-11 year olds, with a focus on grammar, pronunciation, and conversation skills.

pro_course_detail.title: WRITING COACH — COLLEGE ESSAYS
pro_course_detail.description:
This is an intensive class for (1) university or high school students at the C1/C2 level who want guidance and coaching while writing academic essays or applying to college, or for (2) writers for whom English is not their native language. I will share my passion for writing and storytelling, and help you level up your writing skills!

Personal essay, creative non-fiction, short stories, novels 📚

📝 Developmental editing: Concept & flow.
📝 Content editing: Big-picture examination of argument/theme/plot to strengthen the structure.
📝 Copy editing: Final proofing for sentence structure & grammar.
 
We begin with a 30-60 minute brainstorming session to help clarify and structure your ideas around the essay prompt; students should come to class with a rough draft, or at least an outline. The focus will be on big ideas and telling your story in the most powerful way possible—whether you're composing a fictional tale or real-life essay.

Then, after you redraft your essay, we will follow up with a 1-hour editing session focused on improving grammar and sentence structure to native-sounding level (this can be undertaken as a live lesson or as edits/detailed comments returned within 48 hours).

Estimate about 1,000 words per hour, which can vary by genre, complexity, level of polish.
